statement: Recent-graduate unemployment minus the all-worker rate >= 2.0 pp in any 2027 quarter (NY Fed College Labor Market, 2027 quarterly)
status_at_phase_end: In 2025 the gap peaked near the threshold early in the year: March 2025 5.8% vs 4.0% (1.8 pp; a record 1.8 pp in April per later reporting), then narrowed to ~0.8 pp in June (4.8% vs 4.0%) and roughly 1 pp in Q3 (5.3% average; all-worker rate ~4.3%, not verified). Underemployment rose to 41.8% in Q3, the highest since 2020. The Q3 update was delayed to December by the federal shutdown, and October 2025 data are missing/estimated.

items.summary: Regional central bank's Q1 2025 update: recent-graduate (22-27) unemployment jumped to 5.8% in March 2025, the highest since 2013 outside the pandemic, vs 4.0% for all workers: a gap of 1.8 pp, just below the 2.0 pp threshold.
items.detail: NY Fed 'Labor Market for Recent College Graduates', 2025:Q1 data; values per Forbes (2025-06-28), Bloc A Today (2025-06-05), Fast Company. Release date approximate (late April 2025; NY Fed Instagram reel 'deteriorated noticeably in the first quarter of 2025').

items.summary: Q2 2025 update: the recent-graduate rate eased to 4.8% in June vs 4.0% for all workers (gap ~0.8 pp), well below threshold. Graduates in computer engineering and computer science had above-average jobless rates.
items.detail: NY Fed tracker, values as reported by Fortune (2025-09-21) citing Yardeni. Release date approximate (early Aug 2025). Later vintages show Q2 2025 average ~5.3% (seasonal/revision differences); single-month value used here.

items.summary: Another regional central bank's analysis: young college graduates (23-27) averaged 4.59% unemployment in 2025 vs 3.25% for all college graduates; the recent-graduate disadvantage has persisted and widened since the late 2010s.
items.detail: St. Louis Fed On the Economy, 'Recent College Grads Bear Brunt of Labor Market Shifts', August 2025 (own CPS definition, not NY Fed; day approximate).

items.summary: Delayed Q3 2025 update: recent-graduate unemployment 'remained elevated' at an average 5.3%; with the all-worker rate around 4.3%, the gap was ~1 pp. Underemployment rose to 41.8%, its highest since 2020.
items.detail: NY Fed social posts 2025-12-19 (chart 'Remained elevated at an average of 5.3 percent in 2025:Q3') and 2025-12-29 (underemployment 41.8%). All-worker Q3 average (~4.3%) inferred from BLS Jul-Sep 2025 rates (4.2/4.3/4.4), not verified on NY Fed chart.

items.summary: October 2025 survey data are missing (federal shutdown) and later estimated by the source, so the Q4 2025 reading carries extra uncertainty. The series covers Bloc A only; Bloc B publishes youth (16-24, excluding students) unemployment but no recent-graduate vs all-worker series on a comparable basis.
items.detail: NY Fed chart notes: 'October 2025 results are estimated due to missing data.' Bloc B NBS youth unemployment not graduate-specific.
